summary: QA planning for gpt-copy-v7 should gate implementation with mocked backend provider tests, frontend schema and component tests, a mocked streaming Playwright smoke path, full backend/frontend command verification, and secret plus generated-artifact hygiene checks. The supplied architecture, domain, QA trap, and approved project rules are sufficient for planning without user input.

proposals.title: Backend contract and provider failure coverage
proposals.summary: Require Rust tests for health without OpenRouter credentials, OPENROUTER_MODEL defaulting, SQLite migrations, conversation and message persistence, validation failures, structured JSON errors, CORS, mocked non-streaming success, mocked provider_not_configured, provider_rate_limited, provider_timeout, provider_invalid_response, streaming success, and interrupted stream behavior. Provider tests must use injected mocks and must never call OpenRouter.

proposals.title: Frontend validation and ChatGPT-style workflow coverage
proposals.summary: Require frontend tests for composer validation and disabled states, sidebar create/select/mobile drawer behavior, transcript markdown and GFM rendering, unsafe HTML/script non-execution, zod rejection of malformed backend responses, visible error state handling, and TanStack Query cache updates after send flows.

proposals.title: Mocked Playwright streaming smoke
proposals.summary: Require one end-to-end smoke test that mocks backend conversation, message, and SSE endpoints, sends a user message through the UI, consumes mocked streaming deltas, displays the assistant response, checks basic desktop/mobile layout behavior, and asserts no browser request targets OpenRouter.

proposals.title: Final verification and repository hygiene gate
proposals.summary: Before CodeDungeon finalization, run backend fmt, clippy, and tests; frontend lint, tests, build, and Playwright smoke; then scan tracked files for OpenRouter secrets and generated artifacts. Completion evidence should only pass when all commands and scans pass or an environment prerequisite is explicitly documented as blocking.

risks.title: Streaming failure can persist partial assistant output
risks.impact: If the backend writes assistant content before the provider stream completes, SQLite can contain incomplete responses while the UI reports an error.
risks.mitigation: Use mocked interrupted-stream tests that assert SSE error signaling and query persistence to confirm no partial assistant message is stored.

risks.title: OpenRouter key or calls can leak outside the backend
risks.impact: Client-side OpenRouter requests, tracked keys, or live-provider tests would violate approved project rules and make local verification dependent on quota and secrets.
risks.mitigation: Keep provider access behind the backend abstraction, mock all automated provider tests, assert Playwright makes no OpenRouter requests, and run a tracked-file secret scan excluding placeholder-only .env.example.

risks.title: Provider error mapping can drift from the domain contract
risks.impact: Incorrect status codes for missing configuration, rate limits, timeouts, or invalid payloads would break predictable frontend error handling.
risks.mitigation: Add backend tests that exercise each provider failure variant and assert exact HTTP status plus error.code values.

risks.title: Generated artifacts can be committed
risks.impact: Tracked SQLite databases, Rust build output, Next build output, node_modules, or Playwright reports can pollute the PR and harm reproducibility.
risks.mitigation: Keep generated paths ignored and run git ls-files checks for backend/target, frontend/.next, frontend/node_modules, frontend/playwright-report, frontend/test-results, and .codedungeon/codedungeon.db.

risks.title: Local toolchain gaps can block final evidence
risks.impact: Rust 2024 support, npm install state, or Playwright browser availability can prevent full local verification even when implementation is correct.
risks.mitigation: Run the command matrix early, distinguish product failures from environment prerequisites, and record any unrecoverable prerequisite blocker in CodeDungeon evidence.

claims.title: Provider behavior must be verified with mocks
claims.summary: Automated tests should reject any dependency on OpenRouter credentials, quota, network availability, or live provider responses unless the user explicitly changes the requirement.

claims.title: Final acceptance includes command and hygiene gates
claims.summary: Backend fmt, clippy, tests, frontend lint, tests, build, Playwright smoke, secret scanning, and generated-artifact scanning are all required before reporting completion.

claims.title: Streaming and error contracts carry the highest QA risk
claims.summary: Rate limit, timeout, invalid response, missing configuration, streaming completion, and interrupted streaming semantics need exact tests because they span provider abstraction, persistence, SSE behavior, and UI error handling.
